cases.value: entered into force for Viet Nam on 11 September 2026
cases.evidence: Viet Nam acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention. The Convention entered into force for Viet Nam on 11 September 2026, so public documents now take the apostille route instead of consular legalization.
The receiving authority processes complete apostille applications in three business days. Incomplete files pause the clock until the missing item arrives.
The fee schedule lists VND 300,000 per document for apostille issuance. Payment is taken when the application is accepted, not at pickup.

cases.value: 8 Le Van Huu, Hanoi, mornings only
cases.evidence: Walk-in filing is accepted at 8 Le Van Huu, Hanoi, mornings only. Afternoon visitors are asked to return the next working day.
Mail applications to PO Box 40271, Hanoi. Enclose prepaid return postage or the file is held for pickup.
The authentication desk answers status questions at +84-24-3799-1234 during office hours. Written queries go through the ministry portal.
Applications must use Form LS-04, September 2026 revision. Older revisions are returned without review.
Documents executed in Vietnamese need a certified English translation required for the receiving state. The translation is bound to the original before sealing.
Private documents need notarization on the document itself before the apostille is issued. A separate notarial certificate is not accepted.
Counter hours are Mon-Fri 8-11:30 for filing and pickup. The office closes for the midday break and does not reopen counters.
Destinations outside the Convention take a Certificate of Authentication for non-members, which still needs consular legalization after issuance.
Bring one original plus one photocopy of each document. The copy is retained in the file and the original is returned sealed.

cases.value: status table entry for Viet Nam
cases.evidence: The HCCH site shows a status table entry for Viet Nam with the effective date. Routing questions are answered from that entry, not from consular copies.
